evidence.methodology_note: Rubric frozen before scoring this shard. Same rubric structure intended for symmetric application to all 10 languages by the runner when other language shards are merged. Evidence sources: embedded docs/development.md, docs/packages.md, docs/issue-ai-triage.md, docs/spec/* (architecture.md, diagnostics.md, grammar.ebnf, language.md, llm-guide.md, numeric-and-bin.md, patch-schema.md), corroborated where possible by the public quidra-lang/quidra GitHub repository (README, release tags v0.1.0-v0.3.1, merged PRs #1,#3,#4,#5,#6).

quidra_findings: Build system is CMake; the public README documents 'cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release', 'cmake --build build --parallel', and 'ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure' for Unix, plus an analogous vcpkg-based Windows sequence, showing the test runner (ctest) is wired directly into the declared build system.

docs/development.md lists the release check-list: 'GCC and Clang release builds; Linux, macOS, and Windows CI; sanitizer and warnings-as-errors builds; ctest --output-on-failure; parser/checker negative tests; native runtime smoke tests; standard-library and module/import tests; package/version/lockfile tests; REPL/CLI tests; packaging tests; ... documented examples.'

A merged release PR on the live repository states the develop branch had 'passed the repository CI matrix, including GCC/Clang, sanitizers, macOS, Windows, packaging and image dtype coverage,' corroborating the documented CI breadth with an observable artifact rather than only self-reported prose.

A dedicated compatibility CI job continuously tests first-party packages (vision/dnn) against core changes before they land in develop/main, per merged PR #4 ('Add first-party package compatibility CI'), showing build/test integration extends across the multi-repo package ecosystem, not just the core compiler.

Metadata consistency is enforced as an automated, non-optional CI gate: 'python3 tests/metadata_ssot_tests.py ... runs as the quidra_metadata_ssot test, as a no-build metadata job on every push and pull request, and again before a release tag is created.'

CI-safe non-writing verification commands exist for generated artifacts: 'python3 scripts/sync_metadata.py --check writes nothing and exits non-zero when a derived file disagrees'; 'quidra lock FILE.qui --check is the non-writing CI form'; 'quidra fmt FILE.qui --check is the non-writing canonical-form check used by automation.'

Release procedure explicitly gates on green CI and forbids bypassing failing checks: 'Run the complete test suite on develop and require green CI. Fix release blockers on develop; do not bypass failing checks,' and the release workflow itself re-validates metadata and only tags after CI passes on the exact release commit.

Limitation: evaluation is based on documentation and a small number of externally-observable repository artifacts (README build commands, merged PR descriptions, release tags) rather than direct inspection of CI YAML/CMakeLists.txt content, since only docs/ was a readable local path; this caps confidence slightly below a full first-party maximum despite strong, mutually corroborating documented and externally observable evidence of an actively exercised, cross-platform, multi-suite build/test/CI pipeline.
rubric: Standard, reproducible build-system integration (declared build tool, configure/build commands) -- up to 15 pts
Automated test runner integrated with the build system (e.g. ctest) -- up to 15 pts
CI coverage breadth: multiple compilers and multiple OS platforms -- up to 15 pts
Breadth/categorization of test suites (unit/negative/smoke/integration/packaging/regression) -- up to 15 pts
Hardening builds integrated into CI (sanitizers, warnings-as-errors) -- up to 10 pts
Machine-checkable consistency/metadata gates wired into CI on every push/PR -- up to 10 pts
Release-gating discipline (tests/CI required green before merge/tag, documented and enforced procedurally) -- up to 10 pts
CI-usable non-writing '--check' verification forms for generated artifacts (lockfile, formatting) -- up to 10 pts

quidra_findings: A complete formal grammar is published as docs/spec/grammar.ebnf, covering lexical, statement, expression, and type grammar plus explicit static/frontend constraint notes, not just prose description.

docs/spec/language.md is an extensive language reference covering every major feature (types, arrays, bin, classes, generics, enums, references/const authority, tensors, neural/autograd, concurrency, FFI, standard namespaces) with runnable code examples for nearly every construct.

docs/spec/diagnostics.md provides a complete alphabetized table of compiler diagnostic codes with meaning and typical correction for each, plus a documented runtime-failure status/format contract and REPL session-safety error semantics.

docs/spec/architecture.md documents compiler phase ownership/lowering invariants, format-version contracts, REPL/tooling internals, FFI boundary rules, WebAssembly frontend boundary, and native runtime boundary -- internals documentation well beyond a typical user-facing reference.

docs/spec/patch-schema.md documents a versioned, machine-consumable JSON patch schema (with a compiler-served 'quidra describe patch-schema' machine-discovery command) alongside human-readable workflow steps and a diagnostics table for the patch protocol itself.

docs/spec/llm-guide.md is a dedicated 66-rule canonical-generation guide explicitly designed to make LLM-authored code correct on the first attempt, an unusual and deliberate documentation investment.

docs/development.md and docs/packages.md are thorough operational runbooks covering branch roles, semantic versioning policy, the exact numbered release procedure, release checklists, and the complete package-manifest/lockfile/release-identity contract with worked examples.

docs/issue-ai-triage.md documents an additional automation surface (AI-assisted issue triage) including its security boundary, configuration, and label taxonomy, showing documentation coverage extends to auxiliary project tooling, not only the compiler/language.

Deliberate anti-drift discipline is documented and enforced: 'project.toml at the repository root is the single source of truth for project metadata' with a script (`sync_metadata.py --check`) and test (`metadata_ssot_tests.py`) that fail CI if any derived documentation/file disagrees, reducing the risk of stale or contradictory docs that typically erodes documentation-quality scores over a project's life.

Minor gap: no separate narrative 'getting started' tutorial file was present among the embedded docs (only README-level installation commands surfaced via external search), and no explicit versioned changelog file was reviewed, which is why the score is not at the top of the rubric.
rubric: Completeness of formal language reference (types, syntax, full semantics) -- up to 20 pts
Machine-readable/formal artifacts (grammar, schemas) alongside prose -- up to 15 pts
Diagnostics/error and runtime-failure reference completeness -- up to 15 pts
Architecture/internals documentation for contributors and tool authors -- up to 15 pts
Tooling/workflow documentation (build, release, packaging, CI) -- up to 15 pts
Practical worked examples embedded throughout -- up to 10 pts
Documentation maintainability discipline (single source of truth, drift prevention) -- up to 10 pts
